title: AI tool flags fraud frenzy
full_text:
A fraud detection trial using artificial intelligence in the health department's benefits integrity division raised so many red flags that the project was abandoned.
Health officials shelved the project after realising they did not have enough staff to keep up with the volume of suspicious Medicare billing detected, with more than one in five cases flagged proving worthy of investigation and potential prosecution.
The finding is contained in the Auditor-General report on AI in the division, which the Albanese government has tasked with building a new fraud detection system to claw back more of the estimated $2 billion a year wrongly billed by medical practitioners and pharmacists.
Medicare billing expert Margaret Faux said there was a very high risk of Medicare compliance being overwhelmed by AI, saying clearer rules were needed before technology could be effective.
"The problem is that the vast majority of Medicare billing rules are not written down anywhere," Dr Faux told The Canberra Times.
"So it beggars belief that you could think that an AI tool at this stage could apply rules that don't exist.
